chunks: Muhammad narrated from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man performs tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah for nine shawt (circuits), he should count one and discard eight. And if he performs eight, he should discard them and restart the sa'y. And if he starts with Al-Marwah, he should discard what he has performed and start with As-Safa.

key_terms.أَشْوَاطٍ: Shawt, plural of shat, meaning circuits or paces between the two hills
key_terms.السَّعْيَ: Sa'y, the ritual walking between As-Safa and Al-Marwah
key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa, one of the two hills between which Sa'y is performed
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwah, the second hill in the Sa'y ritual
key_terms.لْيَطْرَحْ: He should discard, referring to invalidating extra or incorrect circuits

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim performs an incorrect number of circuits during Sa'y or starts from the wrong place?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi details the specific jurisprudential rules for rectifying errors in the number of circuits during Sa'y, reflecting the Imami school's emphasis on precision in ritual acts. It distinguishes between partial validity (discarding excess circuits) and total invalidity (requiring a restart), particularly highlighting the necessity of starting with As-Safa as the foundational condition for the ritual's validity.
